Mamaji taste of katta is at Opposite ramnarayan ruia autonomous college,L, Lakhamsi Napoo Rd, Dadar East, Matunga East..... Mamaji Taste of Katta in Matunga offers a delightful experience, and their chocolate sandwich is a must-try. Upon entering..... The menu boasts an array of delectable treats, but the chocolate sandwich stands out.

The sandwich is generously filled with rich, creamy chocolate that melts in your mouth with each bite. Mamaji’s Frankies are overall great — the taste and quality are really good. However, there’s room for improvement in a couple of items:

1. Manchurian Frankie: The Manchurian pieces were quite oily, making each bite feel heavy. Reducing the oil content would really enhance the taste.

Hope they take this feedback positively — the rest of their menu is definitely worth trying!

Mamaji Taste of Katta in Matunga offers a delightful culinary experience, and their chocolate sandwich is a must-try. Upon entering, the cozy, welcoming atmosphere immediately sets the tone for a pleasant meal. The menu boasts an array of delectable treats, but the chocolate sandwich stands out.

The sandwich is generously filled with rich, creamy chocolate that melts in your mouth with each bite. The bread is perfectly toasted, providing a satisfying crunch that complements the smoothness of the chocolate. It's clear that quality ingredients are used, making each element of the sandwich taste fresh and flavorful. The balance of sweetness is just right—not too overpowering, yet indulgent enough to satisfy any chocolate lover's cravings.

Service at Mamaji Taste of Katta is efficient and friendly, adding to the overall enjoyable dining experience. The staff is attentive and ensures that orders are served promptly. The ambiance, combined with the excellent food, makes it a perfect spot for a quick snack or a relaxed meal.

In conclusion, Mamaji Taste of Katta’s chocolate sandwich is a delicious treat that shouldn't be missed. Whether you're a local or just passing through Matunga, this spot is worth a visit for its mouthwatering offerings.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently tried the much-hyped batata vada at Shree Krishna Batata Wada in Dadar, and honestly, I was left disappointed. The taste was quite ordinary — nothing extraordinary or unique about it. I had high expectations given the name and long-standing reputation, but the flavor didn’t stand out at all. To top it off, the pricing was shockingly high — ₹27 for just one single vada (not even a plate!). For a simple street snack that’s supposed to be pocket-friendly and satisfying, this felt like a complete rip-off.

There was no chutney or accompaniment that enhanced the taste, and the vada itself lacked spice and crunch. It felt like they were cashing in purely on the legacy or nostalgia rather than actual quality or taste. In a city like Mumbai, where you get amazing batata vadas at countless local joints, this place didn’t meet expectations at all.

If you're a true batata vada lover, I’d suggest exploring other options around Dadar or even in nearby areas — there are definitely better places in terms of both taste and value for money. My honest opinion — a BIG NO to this place. Not worth the hype or the price.

The Matunga Dabeli (obvsly at Matunga from the name) is the definition of 'started from the botton now we're here'. Starting from a roadside stall to establishing themselves to a proper food outlet, they derseve all goodlucks and applause in this journey.
This eatery serves different types of Dabeli and Garlic Paav as the major dishes on the menu, which is a perfect illustration of quality over quantity. .
Although the dabeli is served with peanuts and onions, cheese garlic pav is served with a cheese sliced melted in between the pav which adds to the sharpness of the dish.
Both the delicasies are heated with butter, on a hot tawa (pan) absorbing all the juices and making it cripspier than ever.
The cost of relishing your mouth with the scrumptious delicasises is at pocket friendly price of Rs.20 to Rs.35 each.

Tip:
1. The Garlic paav is an extreme form of spicy gamble. So unless you're sure of handling it without being blown away with all the , inform them
2. It's listed on platforms like swiggy, zomato which makes it a bit trouble - free to get our hands on it.

featured_reviews.name: Jayashri Devadhar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Finally, we got to visit this very popular Dabeli joint at Matunga. Had always heard about it but due it's not so obvious location, had never seen it and hence not visited it.

Just a few minutes from Matunga central railway station and an equal few minutes from the Matunga Circle, Matunga Dabeli is in a little lane and therefore not easily visible when you walk on the main road which has all the temples. However, if you pay close attention or ask a local, it's easily found.

I guess what works here is the simplicity of the dabeli. There's a list of different Dabeli - with cheese, butter, the Dabeli Misal, Jain Dabeli etc., primarily to suit every foodie's specific demand and taste. But what worked for me best was the basic Butter dabeli. Apt Crispiness of the bread made warm on the tawa with butter and just enough of the delicious dabeli filling inside it, makes it perfect for a quick bite when on the move. Pricing is reasonable too.

I'm so glad to have finally visited this one. Will be back again for sure, whenever around Matunga.

Absolutely the worst experience I’ve had at any food outlet.
I visited Matunga Dabili to buy 8 dabilis in parcel, and what happened next was shocking.

The woman at the counter told me to wait 10 minutes. We went to keep our things in the car and returned. While making the payment earlier, I had noticed a white packet lying there for a long time — cold, oily and clearly old. When we returned to collect our order, she brazenly tried to hand me that same stale packet, which had three cold, oil-soaked dabilis, instead of preparing my fresh 8-piece order.

When I asked her to make a fresh batch, both she and the man working there intentionally delayed and rudely said they would finish making 22 dabilis of an online order first. It was very clear they wanted to force us to take the old dabilis that were lying there from God knows how long.

When I asked for a refund, the woman said:
“We won’t give your money back. Once paid is once paid.”

So basically:
•	They didn’t prepare fresh food
•	They refused to refund
•	They tried to push stale food
•	They spoke rudely
•	And proudly said they don’t give anything to beggars or anyone, so we can “leave it and go”

In the end, we had to walk out without the dabilis, and they still kept my ₹240.
No food. No service. No refund. Only arrogance.

This is not how any business should operate.
Selling cold, stale, oily food, forcing customers to take it, refusing refunds, and then being rude on top of it — completely unacceptable.

Avoid this place.
Your health and money both deserve better.

featured_reviews.name: Suryaprakash Barnwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College, Dadar definitely attracts a huge crowd. We reached around 2:15 PM and still had to wait close to 40 minutes in the queue before getting served, which itself shows how popular the place is.

The location is definitely a plus point since it’s close to Dadar Beach. The highlight for me was the crispy chura, which added a unique crunch and gave the vada pav a different texture compared to regular stalls.

However, the overall experience felt a bit overrated for the wait and pricing. The service was slow, there was no extra chutney or extra chura provided, and the vada pavs were simply wrapped in paper and handed over. Since everything is pre-made, there’s almost no scope for customization in terms of chutney or spice level like you usually get at local vendors. Personally, I also found the taste slightly too sweet.

The pricing is ₹35 for a single vada pav and ₹140 for four pieces, which feels almost double compared to many other local vendors offering similar or even better taste.

Overall, it’s worth trying once for the hype and experience, but personally I don’t think the taste and service justify waiting more than 40 minutes when there are plenty of local places serving equally good vada pav with faster service, better customization, and more value for money.

After taking blessings at Shree Siddhivinayak Temple, a visit to Ashok Vada Pav is almost a ritual for food lovers. The vada pav here is served hot and fresh, with a perfectly crispy vada, soft pav, and flavorful chutneys that make every bite memorable.
One of the best experiences is to take a parcel and head towards Dadar Chowpatty. Sitting by the sea, enjoying the view and cool breeze while eating this iconic vada pav creates a combination that's hard to beat. The joy of having Ashok Vada Pav with the sea view is something truly special.
The long queue outside the stall speaks for itself. Just looking at the crowd, you can tell how popular this place is. It's not famous without reason—the taste, consistency, and quality have made it a favorite among Mumbaikars and tourists alike for years.
If you're in Mumbai, this is a must-try street food experience. For many people, Ashok Vada Pav isn't just a snack; it's a part of Mumbai's food culture and one of the most famous vada pav destinations in the city.

I finally tried the famous Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College. Here is my honest take:

The Good part:
• Location: It is located very close to Dadar Beach. It’s nice to grab your order and go for a short walk by the sea.
• Texture: The combination of the vada with the crispy "chura" is definitely interesting and adds a nice crunch.

The Not-So-Good:
• The Wait: Be prepared to stand in line. It took me between 20-30 minutes just to get served.
• Taste & Customization: Because the Vada Pavs are pre-made, there is hardly any room for customization. Unlike other local shops where you can adjust the chutney to your liking, here you get what you get. Personally, I found the taste a bit too salty and sweet for my palate.

The Price:
• ₹30 per piece
• ₹60 for a plate (2 Vada Pavs)

Verdict: While it’s not "bad," I don't think it is worth a 30-minute wait, especially when other local spots offer better customization.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a city that runs on speed, spice, and soul, some places don’t just serve food, they become emotion. Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College is exactly that kind of institution, where generations have stood shoulder to shoulder, waiting for that one perfect bite.
What makes their vada pav truly iconic is the balance. The batata vada is crisp on the outside, soft and flavourful inside, with just the right hint of garlic and spice. The pav is always fresh, lightly toasted, and acts as the perfect carrier without overpowering the star.
But the real magic lies in their chutney game. That signature dry garlic chutney hits instantly with a bold, smoky spice, while the fried green chillies on the side elevate the entire experience. It’s not just heat, it’s character, the kind that lingers and keeps you coming back.
And then comes the cult favourite, the chura pav. Buttery, spicy, slightly messy, and absolutely addictive. The crushed vada mixed with chutneys and masala, soaked into the pav, creates a texture and flavour bomb that feels indulgent in the most Mumbai way possible. Crisp edges, soft centres, and that unmistakable street-style richness.
Being a true Dadarkar, I’ve grown up eating this vada pav, and what’s incredible is how the taste has remained exactly the same over the years, still the best vada pav, hands down.
There’s a legacy here that you can actually taste. Started decades ago and now run by the next generation, Ashok Vada Pav has become a landmark in Dadar’s food scene. It has seen college crowds, office rush, late-night hunger, and everything in between, yet the consistency remains untouched. No unnecessary reinvention, just doing the basics exceptionally well, every single time. The vibe is classic Mumbai, fast-moving queues, minimal waiting despite the crowd, and an energy that feels alive. You don’t come here for luxury, you come here for authenticity.
Ashok Vada Pav isn’t just food, it’s a ritual, a memory, and for many, a weekly craving that never fades.
Simple, iconic, and absolutely unbeatable. 🌶️🔥

featured_reviews.name: Sagar Abichandani
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ (4/5)

Ramashray in Matunga is one of those classic South Indian institutions that still feels properly “Bombay” – bustling, no-nonsense and absolutely focused on the food. I dropped in specifically to try their ghee podi Thatte idli and walked out very happy (and very full).

The ghee podi Thatte idli is easily the hero of the menu. The idli itself is thick and soft – that perfect Thatte style – with a beautiful fermented flavour. It comes drenched in ghee, with a generous ring of podi that clings to every bite. The texture, temperature and seasoning were spot on; this is the kind of dish you could reorder without thinking twice.

The pineapple sheera was another standout. Warm, fragrant and not cloyingly sweet, with enough pineapple to cut through the richness of ghee – it felt like a proper old-school dessert, the kind you’d expect from a place that’s been doing this for decades. If you have a sweet tooth, this is non-negotiable.

Where the experience dipped a bit for me was the masala dosa. For a place with Ramashray’s reputation, I expected a benchmark dosa, but it was underwhelming:
•	The dosa was small in size compared to typical Matunga standards.
•	The texture lacked crispness – instead of that satisfying crunch, the dosa kept crumbling even when handled gently, which made it messy and not very enjoyable.
•	The masala itself was decent, but the base failed to carry it.

Service is fast, efficient and very typical of old-school South Indian joints in Mumbai – you’re seated, served and cleared quickly, which works well given the constant rush. Prices are reasonable for the quality, and the overall vibe is nostalgic: crowded, lively, with conversations, steel plates and filter coffee aromas all blending into one.

Overall, Ramashray still deserves its cult status for certain dishes, especially the ghee podi Thatte idli and pineapple sheera, which I would come back for in a heartbeat. I’m giving it 4 stars only because the masala dosa – usually the litmus test at a South Indian eatery – fell short on texture and portion size. Fix that, and this would easily be a 5-star experience.

⭐ **DP’s Hotel – A Matunga Classic Opposite Ruia College** ⭐
📍 *Matunga East | Opposite Ruia College*

If you're anywhere near Matunga East and your cravings are leading you towards something delicious, flavorful, and comfortingly local – **DP's Hotel** is a name that *needs* to be on your radar. A long-time favorite among college students, families, and foodies alike, this spot has stood the test of time. I dropped by for a casual evening bite, and here’s the lowdown on my experience.

🍛 **FOOD REVIEW**:

🧈 **Pav Bhaji – 4.5/5**
Easily one of the best in town! Rich, buttery, and full of flavor, it strikes the right balance between spice and tanginess. Served hot with toasted pavs, this dish is a total crowd-pleaser. Definitely a must-try!

🍺 **Fruit Beer – 5/5**
An absolute nostalgic winner. Served chilled, this non-alcoholic classic is a throwback to simpler days. Fizzy, sweet, and perfectly refreshing – it complements the spicy food beautifully.

🍯 **Honey Chilli Plum Potato – 4/5**
A delightful fusion starter. Crispy potatoes tossed in a sticky sweet & spicy glaze, with a hint of plum that sets it apart. Would’ve loved it a tad spicier, but still very satisfying.

🍨 **Gadbad (Mangalore Special Dessert) – 3.5/5**
This colorful layered dessert has all the potential to be a star. However, mine I had whe  the ice cream partially melted – which unfortunately dulled the magic a bit. If you're ordering this, make sure it comes straight from the freezer. That said, the combination of fruits, jelly, nuts, and ice cream is still worth trying once!

🏠 **AMBIENCE & SERVICE**:

DP’s isn’t trying to be a fancy fine-dine, but it delivers big on cleanliness and comfort. The vibe is casual, with fast-moving service and staff that are polite and efficient. It’s the kind of place where you can chill with friends, binge on some desi snacks, and leave with a full heart (and fuller stomach).

✨ **PRO TIPS**:

* **Come early in the evening** to avoid the post-college crowd rush.
* **Grab a seat inside** for a more relaxed dining experience – outdoor seating can get a bit noisy.
* **Try their iconic milkshakes and dosas** if you’re coming back for round two – they’re tasty!

Overall, DP’s is a true **Matunga gem**. Consistent, value-for-money, and packed with flavor. Whether you're a first-timer in the area or a long-time local, this spot deserves a visit – and maybe even a second helping.

featured_reviews.name: Aatmi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ayyapan Idli Stall, BKC is a simple, casual, and affordable South Indian restaurant serving authentic vegetarian and Jain food. The focus here is on traditional flavours rather than fancy presentation, and the food speaks for itself. They have self service and each dish is served with coconut chutney, tomato chutney and sambar.

Recommended items:

1. Podi Dosa – A simple yet outstanding dosa coated with aromatic podi and ghee, giving it authentic flavour.

2. Benne Podi Dosa – Soft on the inside, crispy on the outside, and generously layered with white butter and podi, making it rich and satisfying.

3. Thatte Idli – Large, pillowy-soft idli with a light texture that practically melts in your mouth.

4. Medu Vada – Perfectly crunchy on the outside and soft, fluffy, and airy on the inside.

5. Filter Coffee – Strong, aromatic, and authentic South Indian filter coffee with a rich coffee flavour.

A great place for anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian food without spending too much.

featured_reviews.name: KartiK Mittal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ayyappan Idli is a really good spot for authentic South Indian food. We’ve been coming here for years and I think will be the same for many more years to come.

They have moved and taken a bigger place near kings circle station.

This time, we tried their Masala Dosa with cheese which I wish was crispier but had the right amount of filling. The Tatte Idli was soft, fluffy, and the podi is just amazing, the red chutney too, actually all of it is super tasty. The Sada Dosa had a nice crunch. In my previous visits I have also tried gini dosa, medu vada, uttapam.

I really the pineapple sheera—and, of course, their filter coffee was strong, aromatic, and the perfect way to end the meal.

All of this costed us around ₹400 and makes it super affordable and tasty. The place is small, with outside seating but has shade so you wont feel the heat.

They’ve also introduced some new mini idlis, and I can’t wait to try them next time.
You should definitely visit Ayyappan Idli once atleast.

featured_reviews.name: shivani bhanushali
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Ayyapan Idli Eatery for a quick South Indian meal and it didn’t disappoint. The Ayyapan Dosa stood out with its cheesy, flavorful filling – a treat for dosa lovers. The Thatte Idli was the absolute winner; soft idlis generously coated with aromatic podi and ghee, bursting with authentic taste. The Podi Dosa was equally satisfying with its spicy, well-balanced flavors. Tried the Pineapple Sheera to end the meal – while the texture was good, it lacked the strong pineapple flavor I was expecting.

The service was quick, the food came hot, and the pricing felt reasonable for the quality. Overall, a delightful experience and definitely worth revisiting for the idlis!

Lasooni Onion Aloo Kulcha, Cheese Peri-peri Kulcha & the classic Chole Bhature are all time favorites.
